:::{#exr-transpose-product-practice}
#### Transposing a product without reversing the order

@thm-transpose-product says that the [transpose](#def-matrix-transpose) of a [product](#def-matrix-mult) reverses the order of the factors.
A common slip keeps the original order instead,
writing $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$ for $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$.
For two [square matrices](#def-square-matrix) of the same size both products are defined,
so the shapes do not catch the slip.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Does $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$ equal $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$ for these $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compute $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ with @def-matrix-mult and take its [transpose](#def-matrix-transpose),
then compute $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$ and compare the two entry by entry.

:::
